definition: to meet the conditions needed to receive or do something
example: Low-income families may be eligible for the provincial rental subsidy.

definition: to satisfy the conditions needed for something
vi: đáp ứng các yêu cầu, đủ điều kiện
example: Your application was returned because it did not meet the requirements for proof of address.

definition: to formally send a completed form asking for something
example: You can submit an application online or in person at any Service BC centre.
collocations: submit an application before the deadline

definition: how long an office takes to deal with an application
example: Check the government website for the current processing time before you apply for a passport.

definition: a person allowed to live in Canada permanently who is not yet a citizen
example: After three years as a permanent resident, she applied for Canadian citizenship.

definition: an official document that allows a foreign person to work in a country
example: His work permit expires in March, so he is applying for an extension.

definition: to make a document or agreement valid for a further period
example: Don't forget to renew your driver's licence before your birthday.

definition: to come to the end of the time when it can be used
example: My PR card will expire next year, so I need to send in the renewal form soon.
collocations: expire at the end of the month

definition: an identity document from the government, such as a passport or licence
vi: giấy tờ tùy thân do chính phủ cấp
example: Please bring one piece of government-issued ID with your photo.

definition: to send your yearly income and tax information to the government
vi: khai thuế, nộp tờ khai thuế
example: You should file a tax return every year, even with low income, to receive benefits.
collocations: file a tax return on time
late to file a tax return

definition: to have the right to have or do something
example: Employees who work on a statutory holiday may be entitled to time-and-a-half pay.

definition: government payments to people who have lost their job or are on leave
vi: bảo hiểm việc làm, trợ cấp thất nghiệp (EI)
example: After the layoff, he applied for employment insurance while looking for new work.

definition: a rule made by a city or local government
vi: quy định của chính quyền địa phương
example: A city bylaw requires homeowners to clear snow from sidewalks by 10 a.m.

definition: the elected group that makes decisions for a city
example: City council voted to extend library hours on weekends.

definition: a process where the government asks citizens for their opinions
vi: tham vấn ý kiến công chúng
example: The city will hold a public consultation before deciding on the new bike lanes.
collocations: take part in a public consultation

definition: a plan or set of rules adopted by a government or organization
example: The new policy allows nurses to prescribe some medications.

definition: money given for a particular purpose, often by a government
example: The program will close next year unless it receives more funding.

definition: people who pay taxes
example: Critics say the new stadium is a waste of taxpayers' money.

definition: required by a law or rule
example: Winter tires are mandatory on most BC highways from October to April.

definition: following a rule, law or request
vi: phù hợp với, theo đúng (quy định)
example: Your deposit will be returned in accordance with the Residential Tenancy Act.

definition: a formal phrase meaning 'about' or 'concerning'
example: I am writing with regard to the parking permit I applied for last month.

definition: as a reaction or reply to something
vi: để đáp lại, nhằm phản hồi
example: In response to complaints, the city has added more garbage pickups downtown.

definition: to pay money as a punishment for breaking a rule
example: Drivers caught using a phone must pay a fine and also get penalty points.
collocations: be forced to pay a fine

definition: to obey a rule, law or request
example: All restaurants must comply with the new food safety rules by January.

definition: a tax that homeowners pay to the city based on the value of their property
vi: thuế bất động sản, thuế nhà đất
example: Our property tax went up by six percent to pay for new police officers.

definition: basic public systems such as roads, bridges, water and power
example: The federal government will invest in infrastructure to repair flood-damaged roads.

definition: to officially give money or resources for a particular purpose
example: The council decided to allocate $2 million to repair community centres.

definition: to put a plan or decision into action
example: The province will implement the new rental rules next summer.

definition: reductions in the amount of money available to spend
example: Because of budget cuts, the pool will only open five days a week.

definition: papers that prove the information in an application
vi: giấy tờ, tài liệu kèm theo (chứng minh)
example: Applications without the required supporting documents will not be processed.

definition: to write the information that a form asks for in the spaces provided
example: You can fill out the form online and upload your documents instead of going to the office.

definition: a document, such as a utility bill or bank statement, that shows where you live
vi: giấy tờ chứng minh địa chỉ
example: Bring a piece of photo ID and proof of address, like a recent hydro bill, to your appointment.

definition: the legal status of being a citizen of a country
example: After living in Canada for several years, Lan finally applied for citizenship last spring.

definition: to officially choose a person or party in an election
vi: bỏ phiếu trong cuộc bầu cử
example: This fall, my parents will vote in an election for the first time since becoming citizens.
collocations: be eligible to vote in an election

definition: services such as libraries, transit and health care that are provided by the government for everyone
example: Rising costs mean the city may have to reduce some public services or raise taxes.

definition: money the government pays back to you when you have paid more tax than you owe
example: I used my tax refund to pay off part of my credit card balance.

definition: an official document that shows when and where a person was born
example: To apply for your child's passport, you'll need a copy of their birth certificate.
collocations: a copy of a birth certificate

definition: the act of officially telling an organization that you have moved
example: Remember to report your change of address to the Canada Revenue Agency so your tax documents reach your new home.

definition: a secure website where you can log in to use services or see your information
example: You can check your application status anytime through the government's online portal.
collocations: log in to the online portal
upload documents to the online portal

definition: the current stage of an application, such as received, in progress or approved
example: I check my application status every week, but it still says 'in progress'.
collocations: an update on the application status

definition: to be officially accepted or given permission
example: Her work permit was approved after she sent the missing medical exam results.

definition: an application that is missing information or required documents
example: An incomplete application may be returned to you, which can delay the process by several weeks.

definition: a public holiday set by law, when many workers get a paid day off
example: Government offices will be closed on Monday because it's a statutory holiday.
collocations: be closed for the statutory holiday

definition: a person chosen by voters to hold a public position, such as a mayor or councillor
example: Residents should contact their elected officials if they are unhappy with the new parking rules.

definition: the government of a city, town or district, which runs services like roads, parks and garbage collection
example: Local governments are responsible for many everyday services, from libraries to snow removal.

definition: a meeting where members of the public can give their views on a proposal before a decision is made
example: Dozens of residents spoke at the public hearing about the planned apartment tower.

definition: a written request signed by many people asking someone in authority to do something
example: Parents started a petition asking the city to add a crosswalk near the elementary school.

definition: an amount that reduces the tax you have to pay
example: Ask a tax preparer whether you can claim a tax credit for your tuition fees.
collocations: be eligible for a tax credit

definition: money or other help that the government gives to people who need it
example: During the wildfire evacuation, many families received government assistance for hotels and food.

definition: a nine-digit number that you need to work in Canada and to get government benefits
vi: mã số bảo hiểm xã hội (SIN)
example: Your new employer will ask for your social insurance number before your first payday.
collocations: apply for a social insurance number
keep your social insurance number private

definition: the official event where new citizens take an oath and receive their citizenship
vi: lễ tuyên thệ nhập quốc tịch
example: The whole family came to the citizenship ceremony to watch my mother take the oath.
collocations: be invited to a citizenship ceremony

definition: the protection of people from danger, crime and accidents
example: The council says the new street lights are needed for public safety in the park at night.

definition: the national government of Canada, as opposed to provincial or city governments
example: Immigration is mainly managed by the federal government, while health care is run by the provinces.

definition: a person's legal position in a country, such as citizen, permanent resident or temporary worker
example: Some services are open to everyone, regardless of immigration status.

definition: the time of year when people prepare and send their income tax returns
example: Free tax clinics at the library get very busy during tax season.

definition: a public meeting where officials answer questions from local people
vi: buổi đối thoại với người dân
example: The mayor held a town hall meeting to explain the new garbage collection schedule.

definition: services provided by a city or town, such as water, garbage pickup and road repair
example: Property taxes help pay for municipal services like snow removal and street cleaning.

definition: official rules made by a government or organization
example: Food trucks must follow strict health regulations, including regular inspections.

definition: to formally ask someone in authority to change an official decision
vi: khiếu nại/kháng nghị một quyết định
example: If your claim is denied, you have the right to appeal the decision within a set time.
collocations: the right to appeal a decision

definition: the system of rules that controls how land in different areas can be used
vi: quy hoạch phân vùng sử dụng đất
example: The zoning on this street only allows single-family homes, so the developer asked for a change.

definition: a translation of a document that is officially confirmed to be accurate
example: The office asked me to provide a certified translation of my Vietnamese marriage certificate.

definition: the number or percentage of eligible people who actually vote in an election
vi: tỷ lệ cử tri đi bỏ phiếu
example: Voter turnout in the last municipal election was disappointingly low, especially among young people.

definition: to try to be elected to a political position
example: After years of volunteering in the community, Priya decided to run for office on the city council.

definition: to make sure that people obey a law or rule
example: The city has hired more bylaw officers to enforce parking rules downtown.

definition: a law or a group of laws
example: The province introduced new legislation to protect workers who report safety problems.

definition: a person who works for the government
example: As a public servant, Ahmed helps newcomers understand which benefits they can apply for.

definition: official rules and paperwork that seem unnecessary and slow things down
vi: thủ tục hành chính rườm rà
example: Small business owners say there's too much red tape involved in getting a simple permit.

definition: the quality of being open and honest about decisions and how money is spent
example: Residents are asking for more transparency about how the budget for the new arena was decided.

definition: to officially support a relative's application to immigrate and take responsibility for them
example: Tuan hopes to sponsor his parents so they can live with his family in Burnaby.

definition: to start dealing with a problem or illegal activity much more strictly
vi: trấn áp, xử lý mạnh tay
example: The city plans to crack down on illegal short-term rentals in residential neighbourhoods.
collocations: a plan to crack down on

definition: to officially start being used or applied
example: The new recycling rules will come into effect at the start of next year.

definition: to have a document officially signed and stamped by a notary to confirm it is genuine
example: You may need to get the declaration notarized before you send it with your application.

definition: the official power to make decisions and laws, or the area where this power applies
vi: thẩm quyền; phạm vi quản lý
example: This highway falls under provincial jurisdiction, so the city can't fix it on its own.

definition: a complicated system of rules and departments that can make it slow to get things done
example: Many newcomers find the bureaucracy confusing when they first try to get their credentials recognized.

definition: not required to do or pay something that others must
example: Some seniors' housing is exempt from the new fee, according to the city's website.

definition: to introduce a new rule or system gradually, in stages
vi: áp dụng dần dần theo giai đoạn
example: The city will phase in the new parking fees over two years so that businesses have time to adjust.

definition: an official count of a country's population that also collects information about people's lives
vi: cuộc tổng điều tra dân số
example: Information from the census helps governments decide where to build new schools and transit lines.
